t: That the United States Post Office and Federal Building located in Huntington, West Virginia, is hereby designated as the “Sidney L. Christie Federal Building”. Any reference in any law, regulation, document, record, map, or other paper of the United States to such building shall be considered to be a reference to the Sidney L. Christie Federal Building.

fable.w: This section simply names a federal building and directs that references in laws, regulations, and records be read as referring to the new name. The word "regulation" might tempt a Yes reading, but it only refers to existing documents and grants no rulemaking authority. No outside party is consulted, heard, or given a right to object to any federal decision.
fable.s: is hereby designated as the “Sidney L. Christie Federal Building”

opus.w: This section only names a federal building and says how existing references to it should be read. It doesn't involve anyone outside the federal government in any decision: there is no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation or right to sue. The word "regulation" just lists a type of document that refers to the building. It doesn't give anyone authority to make rules, so it doesn't count as participation.
opus.s: Any reference in any law, regulation, document, record, map, or other paper of the United States to such building shall be considered to be a reference to the Sidney L. Christie Federal Building.
opus.b:
1. **Tempting but wrong reading:** The word "regulation" appears, which might look like rulemaking authority. It isn't. The phrase only says that existing references in federal papers to the building now point to its new name. No regulation is authorized or required, and no one outside the federal government is involved.

2. **Label:** No.

qwen_chat.w: The section solely designates a federal building with a specific name and mandates that references to the building be updated accordingly. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or participation with parties outside the federal government. There are no advisory committees, public hearings, or requirements for input from states, tribes, or the public.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that designating a building involves public input or consultation, but the text itself contains no such requirement. It is purely a legislative act of renaming.
